payload.rationale: I estimate a 25% chance using a broad climate-based prior, not a forecast updated with 2026 observations. No outside evidence was supplied. General background knowledge indicates continued human-driven warming, but annual temperatures also fluctuate with ENSO and other natural influences. NASA reported approximately 1.28°C for the exceptionally warm 2024 year, making the contract threshold demanding even with two additional years of underlying warming. The precise event requires the reported, unsmoothed 2026 GISS Land-Ocean Temperature Index to exceed both 1.28°C and the 2025 value; equality with either binding threshold does not qualify. I do not know the applicable 2025 value from the supplied information, so that additional hurdle contributes uncertainty. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that cooler ocean conditions or a high 2025 benchmark could make a qualifying annual average unlikely. The strongest reason it could be too low is that sustained exceptional ocean warmth, an El Niño contribution, or faster underlying warming could substantially increase record-year odds. These are conditional possibilities, not claims about observed 2026 conditions.
limitations: No current research, 2025 GISS annual value, or 2026 monthly observations were supplied.
The estimate cannot incorporate the substantial portion of 2026 already elapsed by the information cutoff.
ENSO conditions and other short-term climate influences are not established by the available evidence.
Settlement depends on the contract-defined NASA GISS series and its reported precision, not another temperature dataset or a rounded news headline.
